idiom: hit the nail on the head
meaning: to describe or identify exactly the right thing or the exact cause of a problem
literal_translation: acertar exactamente al decir algo correcto, dar en el punto justo
example: Your comment about the budget really hit the nail on the head.
origin: Probably from carpentry, when a hammer strikes the nail squarely; the exact origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hammer a nail into a wall
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal meaning, while the idiom is about being exactly right in what you say

wrong_meanings.meaning: to make a mistake and fail completely
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes success in accuracy, not failure
The idiom is about precision in an opinion, not about quarrelling

explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' means to say or identify exactly what is true or the real cause of something. It is often used when someone gives a precise opinion or diagnosis.
